current_answer: Current evidence supports four separate choices: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted, context-carrying WebRTC session now listed at $0.08 per generated second; Reactor FastH3 has separate build and playout queues, hard-cut clips, and a source-stated roughly 15-second build taking about 15.5 seconds on four B200 GPUs or 12.9 seconds on eight; FastVideo FastH3 Preview has local clip routes; and Comfy’s optimized H3 route broadens local access. No low-cost, independently proven setup delivers continuous context at viewer speed.

catalogue_card.question: Do four B200s make FastH3 real time?
catalogue_card.text: Not by the project’s current 15-second example: its FastH3 README says about 15.5 seconds on four B200s and 12.9 on eight. Ready-clip playout still is not a viewer prompt appearing now.

summary: Reactor’s current FastH3 README gives a roughly 15-second build at about 15.5 seconds on four B200 GPUs and 12.9 seconds on eight. These are project-reported conditions, not pool measurements.
The supplied streaming client enables autoplay and idle filler, which can move already-ready clips quickly but cannot remove a build wait, a drained queue, or FastH3’s hard scene boundary.
fal’s H3 Max Director page now lists $0.08 per generated second, a $4.80 60-second minimum, and a stated $72 full 15-minute public-session generated-video spend.
A new-to-the-pool community 5090 report gives roughly 15 seconds at 768×1024 in about 22 minutes with 64 GB RAM under stated settings. It is an offline lead, not a hardware promise or a live result.
A current ComfyUI development-version issue reports higher VRAM pressure and interrupted H3 work on a 5090 D; treat version and launch conditions as part of every local-H3 recommendation.
uncertainty: Reactor’s playout, continuity, and four- or eight-B200 timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
The local 5090 report and ComfyUI development-version issue are individual community reports, not general compatibility, quality, or performance evidence.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
freshness_note: Checked 14 September 2026. FastH3 implementation conditions, local workflow versions, and fal pricing can change quickly; four- and eight-B200 build figures are project documentation, not pool measurements.
